newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmenistan raises state grain procurement price.
newsitem.headline: Turkmenistan raises state grain procurement price.

text.p: Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov has raised some state procurement prices after disastrous grain and cotton harvests last year, the government said on Monday.
The official Turkmenpress news agency said a Niyazov decree had raised the average price the government will pay for grain to 400,000 manats per tonne from 130,000 manats.
The move aims to increase output, the decree said.
The authorities in the largely desert state of 3.8 million are worried about grain shortages.
Last year's grain harvest was a meagre 400,000 tonnes, way below official forecasts of 1.2 million tonnes and far below the 1.0 million harvested in 1995.
Last week Niyazov, the republic's former Communist party boss who is intent on making the country self-sufficient in grain, promised the nation a subsidised monthly ration of flour.
Rations would be eight kilos in the countryside and six kilos in towns.
Another presidential decree aims to boost the country's cotton harvest, one of its main hard-currency earners.
Last year cotton output plummeted to 430,000 tonnes from 1.3 million in 1995.
